title: Rectangular block
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0972]. On the first face, draw a 2D sketch consisting of a rectangular loop made up of four lines. The first line starts at the origin [0.0, 0.0] and ends at [0.75, 0.0]. The second line starts at [0.75, 0.0] and ends at [0.75, 0.0208]. The third line starts at [0.75, 0.0208] and ends at [0.0, 0.0208]. The fourth line completes the rectangle by starting at [0.0, 0.0208] and ending at the origin [0.0, 0.0]. Apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translate it using the same translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0972]. Extrude the sketch 0.0972 units in the direction opposite to the normal, ensuring that this operation creates a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular block are 0.75 units in length, 0.0208 units in width, and 0.0972 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch for the rectangular cross-section
sketch = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0)
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0)
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0208)
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0208)
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0)
    .close()
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical rod with the rectangular cross-section
extruded_part = sketch.extrude(0.0972, both=False)

# Assign the final model to the variable 'r'
r = extruded_part

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0208, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0208, 0.0972) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0972) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
